Surah al-Mujadila is Madani

[Al-Durr al-Manthur, vol. 8, p. 69: Ibn al-Durays, al-Nahhas, Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azhama, and al-Bayhaqi narrate from Ibn Abbas that he said: "Surat al-Mujadila was revealed in Medina." Ibn Mardawayh narrates a similar report from Ibn al-Zubayr, and Allah knows best.]

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of the woman who pleads with you concerning her husband﴾ (the verse). It was revealed concerning Khawlah bint Tha'labah, who was married to Aws ibn al-Samit. She was of good physique, but he had a touch of madness (lamam). He desired her, but she refused him. So he said to her, "You are to me like the back of my mother" (anti 'alayya ka-zahri ummi). Then he regretted what he had said. Zihar and iyla' were among the divorces of the people of the Jahiliyyah. He said to her, "I do not think you are anything but forbidden to me." She said, "By Allah, that is not a divorce." She came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while 'Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) was washing one side of his head, and said, "O Messenger of Allah, my husband Aws ibn al-Samit married me when I was a young woman, wealthy, with property and family. But when he consumed my wealth, wore out my youth, my family scattered and my age grew, he made zihar against me, and now he regrets it. Is there anything that could unite me with him and revive me through it?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "You have become forbidden to him." She said, "O Messenger of Allah, by He who revealed the Book to you, he did not mention divorce, and he is the father of my children and the dearest of people to me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "You have become forbidden to him." She said, "I complain to Allah of my poverty and my loneliness. My companionship with him has been long, and I have borne him children." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "I see you are nothing but forbidden to him, and I have not been commanded regarding your matter in anything." She kept arguing with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and whenever he said to her, "You have become forbidden to him," she would cry out and say, "I complain to Allah of my poverty and the severity of my condition. I have young children: if I gather them to him, they are lost, and if I gather them to me, they go hungry." She kept lifting her head to the sky and saying, "O Allah, I complain to You. O Allah, then send down [revelation] upon the tongue of Your Prophet." This was the first zihar in Islam.

'Aisha got up to wash the other side of his head and said, "Look into my matter, may Allah make me your ransom, O Prophet of Allah." 'Aisha said, "Cut short your speech and your arguing. Do you not see the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" When revelation came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he would be seized by something like a swoon (al-subat). When the revelation had ended, he said to her, "Call your husband," and she called him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to him, "Allah has certainly heard the statement of the woman who pleads with you," and the verses that follow. [Narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir, vol. 2, p. 277, and authenticated by al-Hakim, vol. 2, p. 481. See also Tafsir Ibn Kathir, vol. 4, p. 319.]

'Aisha said, "Blessed is He whose hearing encompasses all voices. Indeed the woman was conversing with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while I was in a corner of the house, hearing some of her words and some of them being hidden from me, until Allah revealed, 'Allah has certainly heard...' and the verses." [Narrated by 'Abd ibn Humayd in al-Muntakhab min al-Musnad, p. 438; al-Nasa'i, vol. 6, p. 186; al-Hakim, vol. 2, p. 481. Imam Ahmad narrates it, vol. 6, p. 46, with the wording "Praise be to Allah who..."; and al-Bukhari mentions it in a suspended report in the Book of Tawhid, chapter "And Allah was Hearing and Seeing," vol. 13, p. 327.]

The meaning of His saying ﴿the statement of the woman who pleads with you﴾: she disputes with you, argues with you, and disputes back with you concerning her husband. ﴿And she complains to Allah, and Allah hears your mutual discourse﴾: your exchange of words in return. ﴿Indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing﴾: He hears what she confides to Him and what she entreats Him with, and sees whoever complains to Him. Then He censured zihar, saying: ﴿Those of you who make zihar against their wives﴾.

**﴿Those of you who divorce their wives by zihar (the pre-Islamic formula of likening a wife to one's mother)﴾**. ʿĀṣim recited "يُظَاهِرُونَ" (yuẓāhirūna) here with a ḍammah on the yāʾ, a light ẓāʾ, an alif after it, and a kasrah on the hāʾ. Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū Jaʿfar, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī recited it with a fatḥah on the yāʾ and the hāʾ, a shaddah on the ẓāʾ, and an alif after it. The rest recited it with a fatḥah on the yāʾ, a shaddah on the ẓāʾ and the hāʾ, and no alif.

**﴿They are not their mothers﴾**. That is, those whom they make like mothers from among their wives are not their mothers. The tāʾ in "أُمَّهَاتِهِمْ" (ummahātihim) is in the genitive case as the predicate of "مَا" (mā), and its position is accusative, as in His saying: "مَا هَذَا بَشَرًا" (mā hādhā basharan) [Yūsuf: 31], meaning "This is not a human being." The meaning is: they are not their mothers. **﴿Their mothers are only those who bore them﴾**, that is, their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them. **﴿And indeed they utter an objectionable word and a lie﴾**: **﴿an objectionable word﴾** that is not recognized in the sharīʿah, **﴿and a lie﴾**, falsehood. **﴿And indeed Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving﴾**, He pardoned them and forgave them by imposing the expiation (kaffārah) upon them.

The form of zihar is that a man says to his wife: "You are to me like the back of my mother," or "You are from me, or with me, or by me, like the back of my mother." Likewise, if he says: "You are to me like the belly of my mother, or like the head of my mother, or like the hand of my mother," or says "your belly, or your head, or your hand is to me like the back of my mother," or likens one of her limbs to another limb of his mother's limbs, it is zihar.

According to Abū Ḥanīfah, may Allah be pleased with him, if he likens her to the belly, the private part or the thigh of the mother, it is zihar, and if he likens her to another limb, it is not zihar. If he says: "You are to me like my mother," or "like the spirit of my mother," and he intends by it honour and respect, then it is not zihar unless he intends it. If he likens her to his grandmother and says: "You are to me like the back of my grandmother," it is zihar. Likewise, if he likens her to a woman who is forbidden to him by kinship, by saying: "You are to me like the back of my sister, or my paternal aunt, or my maternal aunt," or likens her to a woman who is forbidden to him by foster-relationship, it is zihar, according to the most sound of the opinions.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 58, verse 3:**

﴿And those who declare their wives unlawful [by zihar] and then wish to go back on what they said, then [the expiation is] the freeing of a neck [a slave]﴾. Then, the ruling of zihar (the pre-Islamic formula of declaring one's wife unlawful to oneself, like the back of one's mother): it is forbidden for the husband to have intercourse with her after the zihar until he makes expiation (kaffarah), and the expiation becomes obligatory through returning (al-'awd) after the zihar, based on the words of the Exalted: ﴿then they wish to go back on what they said, then [the expiation is] the freeing of a neck﴾.

The scholars differed concerning "al-'awd" (return). The People of the Literal Meaning (Ahl al-Zahir) said: it is the repetition of the word of zihar. This is the view of Abu al-'Aliyah, based on the Exalted's words: ﴿then they wish to go back on what they said﴾, meaning, to what they said [i.e., they repeated it once more]. [The words between the brackets are omitted from "a".] If he does not repeat the utterance, then there is no expiation upon him.

Some people held that the expiation becomes obligatory by the zihar itself, and that the meaning of "al-'awd" is: returning to what they used to do in the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic period) by means of the zihar itself. This is the view of Mujahid and al-Thawri.

Some others said: the meaning of "al-'awd" is intercourse (al-wat'). This is the view of al-Hasan, Qatadah, Tawus and al-Zuhri, and they said: there is no expiation upon him as long as he has not had intercourse with her. [155/b] Others said: it is the intention (al-'azm) to have intercourse, and this is the view of Malik and the companions of the opinion (Ashab al-Ra'y).

Al-Shafi'i held that al-'awd is that he keeps her (as a wife) immediately after the zihar for a period of time in which he could have separated from her, but he did not do so. If he divorces her immediately after the zihar, or one of them dies at that moment, then there is no expiation upon him, because returning to the words (al-'awd lil-qawl) is contradicting them (al-mukhalafah). Ibn 'Abbas explained "al-'awd" as regret (al-nadam), saying: they regret and return to harmony (al-ulfah), and this is its meaning.

Al-Farra' said: It is said, "So-and-so returned to what he said," meaning, "concerning what he said," and "in the annulment of what he said," meaning: he retracted what he said.

This explains what al-Shafi'i said, because his intention by zihar was prohibition. So when he keeps her in marriage, he has contradicted his statement and retracted what he said, and so the expiation becomes obligatory upon him. He even said: if he makes zihar against his revocable divorced wife, his zihar takes effect, and there is no expiation upon him until he takes her back; if he takes her back, he becomes one who has returned, and the expiation becomes obligatory upon him.

His words [the Exalted's]: ﴿the freeing of a neck before they touch one another﴾. The meaning of "al-tamass" (touching) is sexual intercourse (al-mujami'ah). So it is not lawful for the one who made zihar to have intercourse with the wife he made zihar with until he makes expiation, whether he intends the expiation by manumission, by fasting, or by feeding [the poor]. According to Malik, if he intends the expiation by feeding, it is permissible for him to have intercourse before it, because Allah the Exalted restricted manumission and fasting with "before touching," and said concerning feeding: ﴿so whoever is not able, [let him feed sixty needy persons]﴾, and He did not say "before they touch one another." According to the others, the unrestricted wording concerning feeding is to be understood in light of the restricted wording concerning manumission and fasting.

They differed concerning the prohibition of what is other than intercourse among the forms of physical contact before the expiation, such as kissing and enjoyment (al-taladhdhudh). Most of them held that only intercourse is prohibited; this is the view of al-Hasan and Sufyan al-Thawri, and the more apparent of al-Shafi'i's two opinions, just as menstruation prohibits intercourse but not the other forms of enjoyment.

Some of them held that it is prohibited, because the term "al-tamass" includes all of them. If the one who made zihar has intercourse before the expiation, he disobeys Allah the Exalted, and the expiation remains upon his obligation. It is not permissible for him to return [to her] before he makes expiation, and no second expiation becomes obligatory by the intercourse. Some scholars said: if he has intercourse with her before the expiation, two expiations become obligatory upon him.

The expiation for zihar is graded: it is obligatory upon him to free a believing slave; if he does not find one, then he must fast two consecutive months; if he breaks the fast by one day deliberately, or forgets the intention, he must begin the two months afresh; if he is unable to fast, he must feed sixty needy persons. We have mentioned in Surah al-Ma'idah the amount that each needy person is to be fed. [Al-Farra', Ma'ani al-Qur'an: 3/91.]

﴿That is what you are admonished with﴾, you are commanded with it. ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 58, verse 4:

﴿And whoever does not find [a slave]﴾, meaning the neck (raqabah), ﴿then [he must fast] two consecutive months before they touch one another﴾. If he has a slave but needs his service, or he has the price of a slave but needs it for his own maintenance and the maintenance of his dependants, then he may move on to fasting. Malik and al-Awza'i said: he is obligated to free a slave if he has a slave or its price, even if he needs it. Abu Hanifah said: if he has the actual slave, it is obligatory for him to free it even if he needs it; but if he has the price of a slave and needs it, then he may fast. If the one who made zihar began fasting two months and then had intercourse during the month by night, he has disobeyed Allah the Exalted by placing intercourse before the expiation, but he is not obliged to begin the two months again. According to Abu Hanifah, he is obliged to begin the two months again.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿But whoever is unable [to do that], then [he must feed] sixty needy persons﴾, meaning: the one who made zihar, if he is unable to fast because of illness, old age, or intense desire such that he cannot refrain from intercourse, it is obligatory upon him to feed sixty needy persons.

Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharaqi informed us; Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah al-Taysafuni informed us; 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar al-Jawhari informed us; Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Kushmihani narrated to us; 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us; Isma'il ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Harmalah, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, that Khawlah bint Tha'labah was married to Aws ibn al-Samit, and he made zihar against her, and he had a condition of lamam (a touch of madness). So she came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Aws has made zihar against me," and she mentioned that he had lamam. She said: "By Him who sent you with the truth, I have come to you only out of mercy for him; indeed he has benefits from me." So the Qur'an was revealed concerning both of them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Tell him to free a slave." She said: "By Him who sent you with the truth, he does not have a slave nor the price of one." He said: "Tell him to fast two consecutive months." She said: "By Him who sent you with the truth, if you impose three days on him he would not be able." He said: "Tell him to feed sixty needy persons." She said: "By Him who sent you with the truth, he is not able to do that." He said: "Tell him to go to so-and-so son of so-and-so, for he has told me that he has half a measure of dates as charity; let him take it as charity and then give it to sixty needy persons." [[Recorded by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 7/389, and it has a supporting report with Imam Ahmad: 6/410; and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/241. al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/71 added its attribution to Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Mardawayh.]]

And Sulayman ibn Yasar narrated from Salamah ibn Sakhr, who said: "I was a man who had intercourse with women more than others did. When the month of Ramadan came, I feared that I would have intercourse with my wife during it, so I made zihar against her until the month of Ramadan would end. Then one night, while she was talking with me, something of her was uncovered for me, and I did not delay before I had intercourse with her. I went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him, and he said: 'Are you in that state?' I said: 'I am in that state'—he said it three times—I said: 'I am in that state, and here I am, so judge me by the judgement of Allah, for I am patient with that.' He said: 'Then free a slave.' I struck the side of my neck with my hand and said: 'No, by Him who sent you with the truth, I do not own anything other than it.' He said: 'Then fast two consecutive months.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, has what happened to me been caused by anything other than fasting?' He said: 'Then feed sixty needy persons.' I said: 'By Him who sent you with the truth, we spent this night of ours hungry, with no supper for us.' He said: 'Go to the official of the charity of Banu Zuraiq and tell him to give it to you, and feed sixty needy persons from it on your behalf a wasq, then use the rest for yourself and your dependants.'" He said: "So I returned to my people and said: 'I found among you constriction and bad opinion, and I found with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) abundance and blessing. He has ordered that your charity be given to me, so give it to me.' So they gave it to him." [[Recorded by Abu Dawud in al-Talaq, chapter on zihar: 3/137–139; al-Tirmidhi in al-Tafsir: 9/188–191, and he said: "This is a hasan hadith. Muhammad ibn Isma'il said: Sulayman ibn Yasar did not, in my view, hear from Salamah ibn Sakhr." Also 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 6/431; Ibn Majah in al-Talaq, chapter on zihar, no. (2062) 1/665–666; al-Darimi: 2/163–164; al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 7/390; Imam Ahmad: 5/436; and al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/203 on the condition of Muslim, and al-Dhahabi agreed. See: Talkhis al-Habir: 3/221, and al-Albani authenticated it in Irwa' al-Ghalil: 7/176–179.]]

﴿That is so that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning: so that you may affirm what the Messenger (ﷺ) brought from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿And these are the limits of Allah﴾, meaning what has been described of the expiations for zihar. ﴿And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is for the one who denies it and rejects it.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 58, verse 5–6:

﴿Indeed, those who oppose (yuhadduna) Allah and His Messenger﴾ means: those who are hostile to (yu'adduna) Allah and His Messenger, and who oppose (yushaqqquna) and contradict (yukhalifuna) their command. ﴿Will be humiliated (kubitu)﴾ means: they will be disgraced, degraded, and destroyed. ﴿As those before them were humiliated. And We have already sent down clear signs, and for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.﴾ ﴿On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all and inform them of what they did. Allah has enumerated it﴾ means: Allah has preserved their deeds. ﴿And they forgot it, but Allah is Witness over all things.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 58, verse 5–6:

﴿Indeed, those who oppose (yuhadduna) Allah and His Messenger﴾ means: those who are hostile to (yu'adduna) Allah and His Messenger, and who oppose (yushaqqquna) and contradict (yukhalifuna) their command. ﴿Will be humiliated (kubitu)﴾ means: they will be disgraced, degraded, and destroyed. ﴿As those before them were humiliated. And We have already sent down clear signs, and for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.﴾ ﴿On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all and inform them of what they did. Allah has enumerated it﴾ means: Allah has preserved their deeds. ﴿And they forgot it, but Allah is Witness over all things.﴾

[156a] Abu Ja'far read *takūnu* (تَكُونُ) with a *tā'*, because *najwā* (نَجْوَى, "secret conversation") is feminine. The others read *yakūnu* (يَكُونُ) with a *yā'*, because of the *hā'il* (حَائِل, the intervening word between the verb and its subject), which is why the verb is not made feminine.

﴿مِنْ نَجْوَى ثَلَاثَةٍ﴾ means: from the secret talk (*sirār*) of three, that is, from private conversation (*al-musārra*). In other words, there is no matter about which a man confides in his two companions ﴿إِلَّا هُوَ رَابِعُهُمْ﴾ by knowledge.

It was also said: the meaning is that there is no secret conversation among three people, whispering to one another, ﴿إِلَّا هُوَ رَابِعُهُمْ﴾ by knowledge, He knows their private talk. ﴿وَلَا خَمْسَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ سَادِسُهُمْ وَلَا أَدْنَى مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَلَا أَكْثَرَ إِلَّا هُوَ مَعَهُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كَانُوا﴾. Ya'qub read *akthara* (أَكْثَرَ) in the nominative, *akthuru* (أَكْثَرُ), on the basis of the grammatical position of the phrase before *min* (مِنْ, "from") was attached.

﴿ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِمَا عَمِلُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾

﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ نُهُوا عَنِ النَّجْوَى﴾ It was revealed concerning the Jews and the hypocrites. The reason was that they used to hold secret talks among themselves, excluding the believers, and they would look at the believers and wink at one another, giving the believers the impression that they were conferring about something that would grieve them. The believers would be saddened by this and say: "We think that news has reached them about our brothers who went out on the expeditions (*sarāyā*): killing, death, or defeat." This would weigh on their hearts and grieve them. When this went on for a long time and became frequent, they complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he commanded them not to hold secret talks excluding the Muslims. But they did not desist and returned to their private conferences. So Allah revealed: "Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret talk?" [[Refer to: al-Tabari: 28/13; Ibn Kathir: 4/324; al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/80; and al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul: p. 474.]]

﴿ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِمَا نُهُوا عَنْهُ﴾ meaning they return to the private conferences that they were forbidden from.

﴿وَيَتَنَاجَوْنَ﴾ al-A'mash and Hamzah read *wa-yantanjūna* (وَيَنْتَنْجُونَ), on the pattern *yaftaʿilūna* (يَفْتَعِلُونَ). The others read *yatanājawna* (يَتَنَاجَوْنَ), on the basis of His saying: ﴿إِذَا تَنَاجَيْتُمْ فَلَا تَتَنَاجَوْا بِالْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ وَمَعْصِيَةِ الرَّسُولِ﴾. The reason is that the Prophet (ﷺ) had forbidden them from secret talk, but they disobeyed him.

﴿وَإِذَا جَاءُوكَ حَيَّوْكَ بِمَا لَمْ يُحَيِّكَ بِهِ اللَّهُ﴾ The reason is that the Jews used to come in to the Prophet (ﷺ) ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾ "as-sāmu ʿalayk" (السَّامُ عَلَيْكَ). *As-sām* (السَّام) means death. They were giving him the impression that they were saying "as-salāmu ʿalayk" (السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ, "peace be upon you"). The Prophet (ﷺ) would return the greeting by saying "ʿalaykum" (عَلَيْكُمْ, "and upon you"). When they left, they said to themselves: ﴿لَوْلَا يُعَذِّبُنَا اللَّهُ بِمَا نَقُولُ﴾, meaning: "If he were truly a prophet, Allah would punish us for what we say." Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿حَسْبُهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ يَصْلَوْنَهَا فَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾.

[156a] Abu Ja'far read *takūnu* (تَكُونُ) with a *tā'*, because *najwā* (نَجْوَى, "secret conversation") is feminine. The others read *yakūnu* (يَكُونُ) with a *yā'*, because of the *hā'il* (حَائِل, the intervening word between the verb and its subject), which is why the verb is not made feminine.

﴿مِنْ نَجْوَى ثَلَاثَةٍ﴾ means: from the secret talk (*sirār*) of three, that is, from private conversation (*al-musārra*). In other words, there is no matter about which a man confides in his two companions ﴿إِلَّا هُوَ رَابِعُهُمْ﴾ by knowledge.

It was also said: the meaning is that there is no secret conversation among three people, whispering to one another, ﴿إِلَّا هُوَ رَابِعُهُمْ﴾ by knowledge, He knows their private talk. ﴿وَلَا خَمْسَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ سَادِسُهُمْ وَلَا أَدْنَى مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَلَا أَكْثَرَ إِلَّا هُوَ مَعَهُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كَانُوا﴾. Ya'qub read *akthara* (أَكْثَرَ) in the nominative, *akthuru* (أَكْثَرُ), on the basis of the grammatical position of the phrase before *min* (مِنْ, "from") was attached.

﴿ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِمَا عَمِلُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾

﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ نُهُوا عَنِ النَّجْوَى﴾ It was revealed concerning the Jews and the hypocrites. The reason was that they used to hold secret talks among themselves, excluding the believers, and they would look at the believers and wink at one another, giving the believers the impression that they were conferring about something that would grieve them. The believers would be saddened by this and say: "We think that news has reached them about our brothers who went out on the expeditions (*sarāyā*): killing, death, or defeat." This would weigh on their hearts and grieve them. When this went on for a long time and became frequent, they complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he commanded them not to hold secret talks excluding the Muslims. But they did not desist and returned to their private conferences. So Allah revealed: "Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret talk?" [[Refer to: al-Tabari: 28/13; Ibn Kathir: 4/324; al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/80; and al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul: p. 474.]]

﴿ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِمَا نُهُوا عَنْهُ﴾ meaning they return to the private conferences that they were forbidden from.

﴿وَيَتَنَاجَوْنَ﴾ al-A'mash and Hamzah read *wa-yantanjūna* (وَيَنْتَنْجُونَ), on the pattern *yaftaʿilūna* (يَفْتَعِلُونَ). The others read *yatanājawna* (يَتَنَاجَوْنَ), on the basis of His saying: ﴿إِذَا تَنَاجَيْتُمْ فَلَا تَتَنَاجَوْا بِالْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ وَمَعْصِيَةِ الرَّسُولِ﴾. The reason is that the Prophet (ﷺ) had forbidden them from secret talk, but they disobeyed him.

﴿وَإِذَا جَاءُوكَ حَيَّوْكَ بِمَا لَمْ يُحَيِّكَ بِهِ اللَّهُ﴾ The reason is that the Jews used to come in to the Prophet (ﷺ) ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾ "as-sāmu ʿalayk" (السَّامُ عَلَيْكَ). *As-sām* (السَّام) means death. They were giving him the impression that they were saying "as-salāmu ʿalayk" (السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ, "peace be upon you"). The Prophet (ﷺ) would return the greeting by saying "ʿalaykum" (عَلَيْكُمْ, "and upon you"). When they left, they said to themselves: ﴿لَوْلَا يُعَذِّبُنَا اللَّهُ بِمَا نَقُولُ﴾, meaning: "If he were truly a prophet, Allah would punish us for what we say." Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿حَسْبُهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ يَصْلَوْنَهَا فَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾.

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il [al-Bukhari] narrated to us: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us: Abu Ayyub narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Aishah: "The Jews came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, 'As-sāmu ʿalayk.' He said, 'And upon you.' Aishah said, 'As-sāmu ʿalaykum, and may Allah curse you and be angry with you.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, 'Gently, O Aishah. Upon you is gentleness, and beware of harshness and obscenity.' She said, 'Did you not hear what they said?' He said, 'Did you not hear what I said? I returned their greeting, and my prayer for them is answered, while their prayer against me is not answered.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Da'awat, chapter on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "It is answered for us concerning the Jews, but it is not answered for them concerning us": 11/199–200; and the author (al-Baghawi) in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/270–271.]]

Then Allah, exalted is He, forbade the believers from conferring privately among themselves in the manner of the hypocrites and the Jews. He said: ﴿O you who believe, when you confer privately, do not confer in sin, transgression, and disobedience to the Messenger﴾, meaning, do not act as the hypocrites and the Jews do. Muqatil said: by His words "who believe" He meant the hypocrites, that is, those who believed with their tongues. ʿAta said: He means those who believed in their own claim. He said to them: ﴿do not confer in sin, transgression, and disobedience to the Messenger, but confer in righteousness and piety, and fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered.﴾ ﴿Secret conferring is only from Satan﴾, meaning it is from Satan's adornment, ﴿to grieve those who believe﴾, meaning he only makes it appealing to them in order to grieve the believers. ﴿And it cannot harm them at all﴾, meaning the private conferring. It was also said: Satan cannot harm them at all ﴿except by Allah's permission. And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾

Abu Saʿid ʿAbdullah ibn Ahmad al-Tahiri informed us: my grandfather Abu Sahl ʿAbd al-Samad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Bazzar informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Udhafiri informed us: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Dabari narrated to us: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us: Mamar informed us, from Ayyub, from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When there are three of you, two should not confer privately apart from the third, unless with his permission, for that would grieve him." [[Recorded by Muslim in the Book of Greetings (al-Salam), chapter on the prohibition of two people conferring apart from a third without his consent, no. 2184: 4/1718; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/90.]]

Then Allah, exalted is He, forbade the believers from conferring privately among themselves in the manner of the hypocrites and the Jews. He said: ﴿O you who believe, when you confer privately, do not confer in sin, transgression, and disobedience to the Messenger﴾, meaning, do not act as the hypocrites and the Jews do. Muqatil said: by His words "who believe" He meant the hypocrites, that is, those who believed with their tongues. ʿAta said: He means those who believed in their own claim. He said to them: ﴿do not confer in sin, transgression, and disobedience to the Messenger, but confer in righteousness and piety, and fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered.﴾ ﴿Secret conferring is only from Satan﴾, meaning it is from Satan's adornment, ﴿to grieve those who believe﴾, meaning he only makes it appealing to them in order to grieve the believers. ﴿And it cannot harm them at all﴾, meaning the private conferring. It was also said: Satan cannot harm them at all ﴿except by Allah's permission. And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾

Abu Saʿid ʿAbdullah ibn Ahmad al-Tahiri informed us: my grandfather Abu Sahl ʿAbd al-Samad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Bazzar informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Udhafiri informed us: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Dabari narrated to us: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us: Mamar informed us, from Ayyub, from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When there are three of you, two should not confer privately apart from the third, unless with his permission, for that would grieve him." [[Recorded by Muslim in the Book of Greetings (al-Salam), chapter on the prohibition of two people conferring apart from a third without his consent, no. 2184: 4/1718; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/90.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 58, verse 11:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿O you who have believed, when you are told, "Make room in the assemblies," then make room﴾, [and the rest of the verse]. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: The Prophet ﷺ used to honour the people of Badr among the Muhajirun and the Ansar. One day some of them came, and they had been preceded to the assembly. They stood before the Prophet ﷺ and greeted him, and he returned their greeting. Then they greeted the people [present], and they returned their greeting. They remained standing on their feet, waiting for room to be made for them, but no one made room for them. This grieved the Prophet ﷺ, so he said to those around him: "Stand up, so-and-so, and you, so-and-so." He had them rise from the assembly in number equal to the group of men of Badr who had stood before him. This grieved those who were made to rise from their place, and the Prophet ﷺ noticed the dislike in their faces. So Allah revealed this verse. [Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/81) from Ibn Abi Hatim. See also al-Wahidi, Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 475; Ibn Kathir, Tafsir (4/325).]

Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, and we have mentioned his story in the surah of al-Hujurat. [And His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿O you who have believed, let not one people ridicule another﴾, [and the rest of the verse]. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, because he had a deafness in his ear. Whenever he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the people had got ahead of him to the assembly, they would make room for him so that he could sit beside him and hear what he said. One day he came, and he had missed [a rak'ah of the dawn prayer].

When the Prophet ﷺ had finished the prayer, his companions took their places in the assembly. Each man was stingy with his place, so hardly anyone made room for anyone else. Whenever a man came and found no place to sit, he would stand as he was. When Thabit finished the prayer, he came toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, stepping over the necks of the people and saying, "Make room, make room." They began making room for him until he reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and between him and the Prophet there was a man. He said to him, "Make room." The man said, "You have found a place, so sit down." Thabit sat behind him, angry. When the darkness cleared, Thabit nudged the man and said, "Who is this?" He said, "I am so-and-so." Thabit said, "The son of so-and-so," and he mentioned a mother of his for whom he used to be reproached in the Jahiliyyah. The man lowered his head, ashamed, and Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.] Qatadah said: They used to compete for a place in the assembly of the Prophet ﷺ. When they saw someone coming toward them, they were stingy with their place, so Allah commanded them that some of them should make room for others. [Narrated by al-Tabari, 28/17.]

It was also said: This happened on the day of Friday, and then Allah, may He be exalted, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, when you are told, "Make room"﴾.

His saying ﴿O you who have believed, when you are told, "Make room"﴾ means: widen [the space] in the assembly. Al-Hasan and Asim read "fi al-majalis" (in the assemblies), because each one sits in an assembly, meaning: let each man make room in his own assembly. The others read "fi al-majlis" (in the assembly) in the singular, because what is meant is the assembly of the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿Then make room (fafsahu)﴾ means widen [the space]. It is said: fasaha yafsahu fashan, when one widens the space in the assembly. ﴿Allah will make room for you (yafsih Allah lakum)﴾ means Allah will widen for you Paradise and its assemblies within it.

Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Ubayd Allah ibn Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "None of you should make a man rise from his place and then sit in it himself. Rather, make room and widen [the space]." [Narrated by al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad (2/186); al-Bukhari in al-Isti'dhan, chapter "When you are told, 'Make room in the assemblies,' then make room" (11/62); Muslim in al-Salam, chapter on the prohibition of a person making another rise from a permissible place which he has reached first (no. 2177) (4/1714); and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (12/297).]

Abd al-Wahhab ibn al-Khatib informed us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Abd al-Majid informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Sulayman ibn Musa said, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "None of you should make his brother rise on Friday [156/b], but let him say: 'Make room.'" [Narrated by al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad (2/187), and Muslim in the same place (no. 2178) (4/1715).]

Abu al-Aliyah, al-Qurazi and al-Hasan said: This refers to the assemblies of war and the seats of fighting. A man would come to the people in the battle line and say, "Make room," but they would refuse him because of their eagerness for fighting and their desire for martyrdom. [See al-Tabari, 28/17.]

﴿And when you are told, "Rise up," then rise up﴾. The people of Medina, al-Sham and Asim read "unshuzu" (with a damma on the shin), while the others read it with a kasra on both letters. Both are dialects, meaning: rise up. It was said: Rise up from your places until you make room for your brothers. Ikrimah and al-Dahhak said: Some men used to be sluggish about the prayer when it was called, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. Its meaning is: when it is called for the prayer, then rise up for it. [See al-Tabari, 28/18.]

Mujahid and most of the commentators said: Its meaning is: when you are told, "Rise up to the prayer, to jihad, and to the assemblies of every good and truth," then stand up for them and do not fall short. [See al-Tabari, 28/18.]

﴿Allah will raise those of you who have believed﴾ by their obedience to His Messenger ﷺ, their rising from their assemblies, and their making room for their brothers, ﴿and those who have been given knowledge﴾ among the believers, by the excellence of their knowledge and their precedence, [raised to] "degrees." So Allah, may He be exalted, informed that His Messenger ﷺ is right in what he commanded, that those believers are rewarded for what they complied with, and that the group from the people of Badr deserve the honour with which they were treated.

﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾. Al-Hasan said: Ibn Mas'ud recited this verse and said: "O people, understand this verse, and we will encourage you to seek knowledge, for Allah, may He be exalted, says: 'Allah will raise those of you who have believed and those who have been given knowledge by degrees.' The believer who has knowledge is above the one who does not have knowledge by degrees."

[Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: Imam Abu al-Tayyib Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman informed us: Abu Ali Hamid ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Harawi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yunus al-Qurashi informed us: Ubayd Allah ibn Dawud informed us: Asim ibn Raja' ibn Haywah informed us: Dawud ibn Jamil informed me, from Kathir ibn Qays, who said: I was sitting with Abu al-Darda' in the mosque of Damascus when a man came and said: "O Abu al-Darda', I have come to you from the city of the Messenger ﷺ for a hadith which I have heard you narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: "Did you have no other need than that?" He said: "No." He said: "Did you not come for trade?" He said: "No." He said: "And you came only out of desire for it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Whoever takes a path seeking knowledge therein, Allah will make a path to Paradise easy for him for it. The angels lower their wings out of pleasure with the seeker of knowledge. The heavens, the earth, and the fish in the water pray for forgiveness for him. The excellence of the scholar over the worshipper is like the excellence of the full moon over the rest of the stars. The scholars are the heirs of the prophets, and the prophets did not leave behind dinars or dirhams, but they left behind knowledge. Whoever takes it has taken a great portion.'" [Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Ilm, chapter on urging the seeking of knowledge (5/243), and al-Mundhiri said: "This hadith has been greatly disputed..." Also by al-Tirmidhi in al-Ilm, chapter on what has come concerning the excellence of jurisprudence over worship (7/450-453), but through the route of Mahmud ibn Khidash al-Baghdadi, and he said: "We do not know this hadith except from the hadith of Asim ibn Raja' ibn Haywah, and its isnad in my view is not connected in this form: Mahmud ibn Khidash narrated this hadith to us; rather, this hadith is narrated from Asim ibn Raja' ibn Haywah, from Dawud ibn Jamil, from Kathir ibn Qays, from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet ﷺ, and this is more authentic than the hadith of Mahmud ibn Khidash." Also by al-Darimi (1/98); Ibn Majah in the introduction, chapter on the excellence of scholars and urging the seeking of knowledge (223) (1/81); Imam Ahmad (5/196); Ibn Hibban in Mawarid al-Zam'an (p. 48); and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (1/275-276). The hadith has supporting narrations which strengthen it, as the Hafiz said in al-Fath (1/160). Al-Albani authenticated it in Sahih al-Jami', no. 6297.]

[Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us: Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Sarraj informed us: al-Hasan ibn Ya'qub al-Adl informed us: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab al-Farra' informed us: Ja'far ibn Awn informed us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad informed us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Rafi', from Abd Allah ibn Amr, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by two assemblies in his mosque. One of the two assemblies was calling upon Allah and turning to Him in desire, and the other was learning jurisprudence and teaching it. He said: "Both assemblies are upon good, and one of them is better than the other. As for these, they call upon Allah and turn to Him in desire; and as for those, they learn jurisprudence and teach the ignorant. These are better. Indeed, I was sent only as a teacher." Then he sat with them. [Narrated by al-Darimi (1/99-100); Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi (p. 298); and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (1/274-275). The hadith is weak because of the weakness of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad ibn An'am al-Afriqi.]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger privately, spend in charity before your private consultation﴾, meaning before your private conference with him.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The reason was that people questioned the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) excessively, until they wearied him. Allah wished to lighten the burden on His Prophet, to discourage them and deter them from this, so He commanded them to give charity before consulting the Messenger (ﷺ) privately. [[Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/83, from Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh. See also al-Tabari: 28/20-21.]]

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It was revealed concerning the wealthy. They used to come to the Prophet (ﷺ) and consult him privately at great length, and they would crowd out the poor from the gatherings, until the Prophet (ﷺ) disliked how long they sat and consulted him. When they saw this, they desisted from consulting him privately. As for the people of hardship, they had nothing to give, and as for the people of means, they were stingy. This was difficult for the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), so the concession was revealed. [[See: al-Wahidi, Asbab al-Nuzul, p. (476).]]

Mujahid said: They were forbidden from private consultation until they gave charity. No one consulted him privately except 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who gave a dinar (a gold coin) in charity and then consulted him. Then the concession was revealed. 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, would say: "It is a verse in the Book of Allah that no one acted upon before me and no one will act upon after me, and it is the verse of private consultation." [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 28/19-20, and Ibn Kathir: 4/327.]]

It is also related from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called me and said: "Do you not see a dinar?" I said: "They cannot afford it." He said: "How much then?" I said: "A grain or a barleycorn." He said: "You are indeed frugal." Then it was revealed: ﴿Are you apprehensive about spending in charity before your private consultations?﴾ 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "So because of me, Allah lightened the burden on this Ummah." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Tafsir, Tafsir Surat al-Mujadilah, 9/192-194, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith." Also narrated by al-Tabari: 28/21, Abu Ya'la: 1/223, and Ibn Hibban in Mawarid al-Zam'an, no. (1764), p. (437). In its chain is 'Ali ibn 'Alqamah, whom Ibn Hibban mentioned in al-Majruhin (2/109) and said: "He is a munkar al-hadith who narrates from 'Ali what does not resemble his other narrations." al-Dhahabi also mentioned him in al-Mizan (3/146) and said: "There is something to be examined in his hadith," and he cited this hadith which al-Uqayli mentioned in al-Du'afa'.]]

﴿That is better for you﴾, meaning giving charity before private consultation, ﴿and purer. But if you do not find [the means], then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning the poor who cannot find anything to give in charge are pardoned.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 58, verse 13–21:

﴿Are you apprehensive that you should offer charity before your private consultation?﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Are you stingy?" The meaning is: "Do you fear poverty and destitution if you offer charity before your private consultation?" ﴿Then, since you did not do it,﴾ that which you were commanded, ﴿and Allah has turned to you [in forgiveness]﴾ meaning He pardoned you and did not punish you for abandoning charity. It was also said that the "wa" (and) is superfluous (ṣila), its meaning being: "If you do not do it, Allah has turned to you and abrogated the charity." [Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "That lasted ten nights, then it was abrogated."] [[The text between the brackets is missing from manuscript "A".]] Al-Kalbi said: "It was only an hour of the day."

﴿So establish prayer﴾ the obligatory prayer, ﴿and give zakat﴾ the obligatory zakat, ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾

﴿Have you not considered those who have taken as allies a people with whom Allah is angry?﴾ It was revealed concerning the hypocrites who allied themselves with the Jews and advised them and passed the secrets of the believers to them. [[See: al-Qurtubi: 17/304.]] By his saying "with whom Allah is angry" he meant the Jews. ﴿They are neither of you nor of them﴾ meaning the hypocrites are neither among the believers in religion and loyalty, nor among the Jews and the disbelievers, as He said: "Wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those" [An-Nisa: 143]. ﴿And they swear by Allah to a lie while they know [it].﴾ As-Suddi and Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning ʿAbdullah ibn Nabtal, the hypocrite, who used to sit with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and then carry his words to the Jews. While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in one of his chambers, he said: "A man is about to enter upon you now, whose heart is the heart of a tyrant and who looks with the eyes of a devil." ʿAbdullah ibn Nabtal entered, and he had blue eyes. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Why do you and your companions insult me?" He swore by Allah that he had not done so, and he brought his companions, who swore by Allah that they had not insulted him. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed these verses, saying: "And they swear by Allah to a lie while they know" — that they are liars. [[Mentioned by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 476. The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. 165: "I have not found it in this form."]]

﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. Indeed, evil is what they have been doing.﴾

﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield, and so they averted [people] from the way of Allah; so for them is a humiliating punishment.﴾ ﴿Never will their wealth or their children avail them against Allah at all. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾ ﴿On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all and they will swear to Him as they swear to you, and they think that they are upon something. Al-Zajjaj said: The victory of the messengers is of two kinds: whoever was sent with war is victorious by war, and whoever was not commanded to fight is victorious by proof.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 58, verse 13–21:

﴿Are you apprehensive that you should offer charity before your private consultation?﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Are you stingy?" The meaning is: "Do you fear poverty and destitution if you offer charity before your private consultation?" ﴿Then, since you did not do it,﴾ that which you were commanded, ﴿and Allah has turned to you [in forgiveness]﴾ meaning He pardoned you and did not punish you for abandoning charity. It was also said that the "wa" (and) is superfluous (ṣila), its meaning being: "If you do not do it, Allah has turned to you and abrogated the charity." [Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "That lasted ten nights, then it was abrogated."] [[The text between the brackets is missing from manuscript "A".]] Al-Kalbi said: "It was only an hour of the day."

﴿So establish prayer﴾ the obligatory prayer, ﴿and give zakat﴾ the obligatory zakat, ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾

﴿Have you not considered those who have taken as allies a people with whom Allah is angry?﴾ It was revealed concerning the hypocrites who allied themselves with the Jews and advised them and passed the secrets of the believers to them. [[See: al-Qurtubi: 17/304.]] By his saying "with whom Allah is angry" he meant the Jews. ﴿They are neither of you nor of them﴾ meaning the hypocrites are neither among the believers in religion and loyalty, nor among the Jews and the disbelievers, as He said: "Wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those" [An-Nisa: 143]. ﴿And they swear by Allah to a lie while they know [it].﴾ As-Suddi and Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning ʿAbdullah ibn Nabtal, the hypocrite, who used to sit with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and then carry his words to the Jews. While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in one of his chambers, he said: "A man is about to enter upon you now, whose heart is the heart of a tyrant and who looks with the eyes of a devil." ʿAbdullah ibn Nabtal entered, and he had blue eyes. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Why do you and your companions insult me?" He swore by Allah that he had not done so, and he brought his companions, who swore by Allah that they had not insulted him. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed these verses, saying: "And they swear by Allah to a lie while they know" — that they are liars. [[Mentioned by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 476. The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. 165: "I have not found it in this form."]]

﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. Indeed, evil is what they have been doing.﴾

﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield, and so they averted [people] from the way of Allah; so for them is a humiliating punishment.﴾ ﴿Never will their wealth or their children avail them against Allah at all. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾ ﴿On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all and they will swear to Him as they swear to you, and they think that they are upon something. Unquestionably, it is they who are the liars.﴾ ﴿Satan has overcome them and made them forget the remembrance of Allah. Those are the party of Satan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger are among the most humiliated.﴾ "Al-Adhallin" means the lowest. That is, they are among those who will be overtaken by humiliation in this world and the Hereafter.

﴿Allah has decreed: "Indeed, I will overcome, I and My messengers." Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.﴾ [Its parallel is] [[Missing from manuscript "A".]] His saying: "And already has Our word preceded to Our servants the messengers, that they would be those given victory" (As-Saffat: 171–172). Al-Zajjaj said: The victory of the messengers is of two kinds: whoever was sent with war is victorious by war, and whoever was not commanded to fight is victorious by proof.

He, may He be glorified and exalted, said: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers, or their kinsfolk﴾ to the end of the verse. He informed that the faith of the believers is corrupted by showing affection to the disbelievers, and that whoever is a believer does not take as an ally one who disbelieves, even if he is of his own clan.

It was said: it was revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, when he wrote to the people of Makkah. It will come in Surat al-Mumtahanah, Allah willing, may He be glorified and exalted. [[See al-Qurtubi 17/308.]]

Muqatil ibn Hayyan related from Murrah al-Hamdani, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, concerning this verse, that he said: "﴿Even if they were their fathers﴾" refers to Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, who killed his father Abdullah ibn al-Jarrah on the day of Uhud. "﴿Or their sons﴾" refers to Abu Bakr, who invited his son to single combat on the day of Badr, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, let me be in the first journey." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Enjoy us with yourself, O Abu Bakr." "﴿Or their brothers﴾" refers to Mus'ab ibn Umayr, who killed his brother Ubayd ibn Umayr on the day of Uhud. "﴿Or their kinsfolk﴾" refers to Umar, who killed his maternal uncle al-As ibn Hisham ibn al-Mughirah on the day of Badr; and Ali, Hamzah and Ubaydah killed, on the day of Badr, Utbah and Shaybah, the two sons of Rabi'ah, and al-Walid ibn Utbah. [[See: al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 478; al-Qurtubi 17/307; Ibn Kathir 4/330.]]

﴿Those, He has written faith in their hearts﴾: He established the affirmation in their hearts, so they are certain and sincere. It was also said: He judged them to be believers, and mentioned the hearts because they are its place. ﴿And He strengthened them with a spirit from Him﴾: He supported them with help from Him. Al-Hasan said: He called His help to them a spirit, because their affair is given life by it. Al-Suddi said: it means faith. Al-Rabi' said: it means the Qur'an and its proof, as He said: "And thus We have revealed to you a spirit from Our command" [al-Shura: 52]. It was also said: with mercy from Him. It was said: He aided them with Jibril, peace be upon him.

﴿And He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Those are the party of Allah. Unquestionably, the party of Allah are the successful﴾
